verdict.rationale: Sandbox0 documents a refreshable soft `ttl` that keeps a sandbox running while work continues, plus a separate `hard_ttl`. Its session supervisor is meant for background workers and agent runtimes that outlive an SDK call, and pause/resume preserves the RootFS so long tasks can span idle periods. Per-second billing with no one-hour minimum makes long runs practical. missing for 10: an explicit documented maximum runtime confirming multi-hour or multi-day sessions, independent or hands-on corroboration of long-running stability.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep a sandbox session running for hours or days for long agent tasks

citations.quote: claim a sandbox with a soft ttl; refresh the soft deadline while work continues, then let it expire when idle
background workers and agent runtimes that must outlive an SDK call
Preserve the whole writable root filesystem across successful checkpoints, pause compute between tasks, and resume the same sandbox when work returns.
the RootFS expands automatically online as it fills, within the configured device ceiling, while the agent keeps running.
